subject: maths
title: Chapter 7 · Test 2
summary: Chapter 7 test 2: 15 new questions on angles, parallel lines, triangles, quadrilaterals, transformations, symmetry and 3D shapes.
body:
This test covers all of Chapter 7, Geometry: measuring and classifying angles, angles at a point and vertically opposite angles, angles and parallel lines, triangles, quadrilaterals, transformations and symmetry, and 3D shapes and nets.

- **Time:** about 25 minutes.
- **Conditions:** no notes, and no calculator unless the question says. Use scrap paper for working — sketching a quick diagram helps a lot in geometry.
- **Questions:** 15 multiple-choice questions — 4 Easy, 5 Medium, 4 Hard and 2 Challenge.

Read each question carefully and write a reason for each angle you find, such as "angles on a straight line add to 180°". If you get a question wrong, Brainsnacc will show you the step that went wrong, so you know which lesson to go back to.

questions.explanation: 230° is more than 180° but less than 360°, so it is a reflex angle. It is not obtuse, because obtuse angles are less than 180°.
steps: Compare 230° with 180°: it is bigger, so it is not acute, right, obtuse or straight.
Compare 230° with 360°: it is smaller, so it is not a revolution.
An angle between 180° and 360° is reflex.

mistakes.A: Step 2: obtuse angles stop below 180°. 230° is past 180°, so it is bigger than any obtuse angle.
mistakes.B: Step 2: a revolution is exactly 360°, one full turn. 230° is less than a full turn.
mistakes.C: Step 1: a straight angle is exactly 180°. 230° is more than 180°.

questions.prompt: A transversal crosses two parallel lines. Which letter shape helps you spot co-interior angles?
questions.explanation: Co-interior angles are between the parallel lines on the same side of the transversal, which traces a C (or U) shape. The Z shape is for alternate angles.
steps: Co-interior angles sit between the two parallel lines.
They are on the same side of the transversal.
Tracing them gives a C shape.

mistakes.B: Step 2: the F shape shows corresponding angles. Co-interior angles are between the lines on the same side, which traces a C.
mistakes.C: Step 2: the Z shape shows alternate angles (opposite sides of the transversal). Co-interior angles are on the same side.
mistakes.D: Step 2: an X shows vertically opposite angles at one crossing. Co-interior angles use both crossings, on the same side.

questions.prompt: A triangle has sides of 4 cm, 6 cm and 7 cm. What type of triangle is it, named by its sides?
questions.explanation: All three sides (4 cm, 6 cm, 7 cm) are different lengths, so the triangle is scalene. Isosceles would need two equal sides.
steps: Look at the three side lengths: 4 cm, 6 cm and 7 cm.
No two of them are the same.
A triangle with no equal sides is scalene.

mistakes.A: Step 1: an isosceles triangle needs two sides the same length. Check: 4, 6 and 7 are all different.
mistakes.C: Step 1: an equilateral triangle needs all three sides equal. These three lengths are all different.
mistakes.D: Step 2: 'right-angled' is a name by angles, not by sides. The question asks for the name by sides.

questions.prompt: How many vertices (corners) does a square-based pyramid have?
questions.explanation: A square-based pyramid has 4 corners on its base plus the apex at the top: 5 vertices. 4 forgets the apex.
steps: The square base has 4 corners.
There is one more corner at the top, the apex.
Vertices = 4 + 1 = 5.

mistakes.A: Step 2: you counted only the 4 corners of the square base. Don't forget the apex, the point at the top.
mistakes.B: Step 2: 8 is the number of edges. Vertices are the corners — the 4 base corners plus the apex.
mistakes.D: Step 1: the apex is only one vertex. The 4 corners of the square base are vertices too.

questions.prompt: Two arms make an obtuse angle of 140°. What is the reflex angle on the other side of the arms?
questions.explanation: The obtuse angle and the reflex angle together make a full turn, so the reflex angle is 360° − 140° = 220°. 40° uses 180° instead of 360°.
steps: The two angles between the arms make a full turn: 360°.
Reflex angle = 360° − 140° = 220°.

mistakes.A: Step 1: you took 140° from 180°. The two angles go all the way round, so together they make 360°.
mistakes.C: Step 2: the reflex angle is the other way round the vertex. It must be more than 180°, so it can't be 140°.
mistakes.D: Step 2: you added 180°. Instead, take 140° away from the full turn of 360°.

questions.topic: Angles at a point and vertically opposite angles
questions.prompt: Two angles are complementary. One is 34°. What is the other?
questions.explanation: Complementary angles add to 90°, so the other angle is 90° − 34° = 56°. 146° would be the supplementary angle (adding to 180°).
steps: Complementary angles add to 90°.

mistakes.A: Step 1: 146° makes 180° with 34° — that is supplementary. Complementary angles add to 90°.
mistakes.B: Step 1: you took 34° from 360°. Complementary angles add to 90°.
mistakes.C: Step 2: in the units column you did 4 − 0 instead of borrowing. Redo 90 − 34 and check by adding your answer to 34.

questions.prompt: One angle of a rhombus is 64°. What size is an angle next to it (sharing a side)?
questions.explanation: A rhombus is a parallelogram, so angles next to each other add to 180°: 180° − 64° = 116°. 64° is the opposite angle, not the one next to it.
steps: A rhombus has two pairs of parallel sides.
Two angles next to each other are co-interior angles between parallel sides, so they add to 180°.
Angle next to it = 180° − 64° = 116°.

mistakes.B: Step 1: the angle OPPOSITE is equal to 64°. An angle next to it is co-interior between parallel sides, so they add to 180°.
mistakes.C: Step 2: you took 64° from 360°. Two angles next to each other in a rhombus add to 180°.
mistakes.D: Step 2: you took 64° from 90°. Next-door angles in a rhombus add to 180°, not 90°.

questions.prompt: The point (−2, 5) is translated 3 units left and 4 units down. What is its image?
questions.explanation: Left 3 means x goes from −2 to −5, and down 4 means y goes from 5 to 1, so the image is (−5, 1). (1, 1) comes from moving right instead of left.
steps: Left 3 units: subtract 3 from x — −2 − 3 = −5.
Down 4 units: subtract 4 from y — 5 − 4 = 1.
The image is (−5, 1).

mistakes.A: Step 1: you moved right instead of left. Moving left subtracts from the x-coordinate: −2 − 3.
mistakes.B: Step 2: you moved up instead of down. Moving down subtracts from the y-coordinate: 5 − 4.
mistakes.D: Step 1: you used the 4 for x and the 3 for y. Left/right changes x (by 3) and up/down changes y (by 4).

questions.prompt: A right-angled triangle has another angle of 41°. What is the third angle?
questions.explanation: The angles add to 180°, and one is 90°, so the third angle is 180° − 90° − 41° = 49°. 139° forgets the right angle.
steps: The three angles of a triangle add to 180°.
A right-angled triangle has one angle of 90°, so the two known angles are 90° + 41° = 131°.
Third angle = 180° − 131° = 49°.

mistakes.A: Step 2: you took away only 41°. The right angle (90°) is one of the angles too, so take that away as well.
mistakes.C: Step 2: the two smaller angles are only equal if the triangle is isosceles. Use the angle sum of 180° instead.
mistakes.D: Step 1: you used 360°, which is for quadrilaterals. The angles of a triangle add to 180°.

questions.prompt: A transversal crosses two parallel lines. Two co-interior angles are x° and 2x°. Find the larger angle.
questions.explanation: Co-interior angles add to 180°, so 3x = 180, x = 60 and the larger angle is 2x = 120°. 60° is the smaller angle.
steps: Co-interior angles between parallel lines add to 180°, so x + 2x = 180.
Collect the x terms: 3x = 180.
Divide by 3: x = 60.
Larger angle = 2x = 120°. Check: 60 + 120 = 180 ✓

mistakes.A: Step 4: 60 is the value of x, which is the smaller angle. The larger angle is 2x.
mistakes.B: Step 1: co-interior angles add to 180°, not 360°. Use x + 2x = 180.
mistakes.C: Step 2: x + 2x makes 3x, not 2x. Collect the x terms carefully.

questions.prompt: A regular hexagon has rotational symmetry of order 6. What is the smallest angle you can turn it so that it fits onto itself?
questions.explanation: A shape of order 6 fits onto itself 6 times in one full turn, so the smallest turn is 360° ÷ 6 = 60°. 360° works but is not the smallest.
steps: Order 6 means the hexagon fits onto itself 6 times in one full turn of 360°.
Smallest turn = 360° ÷ 6 = 60°.

mistakes.B: Step 2: you divided 180° by 6. A full turn is 360°, so divide 360° by the order.
mistakes.C: Step 2: a full turn always fits, but it is not the smallest. Share the full turn among the 6 fits: 360° ÷ 6.
mistakes.D: Step 2: you multiplied 360° by 6. The hexagon fits 6 times in one turn, so divide instead.

questions.prompt: A prism has 18 edges. What shape is its base?
questions.explanation: A prism whose base has n sides has 3n edges, so 3n = 18 and n = 6: a hexagon. A nonagon comes from wrongly dividing by 2.
steps: A prism with an n-sided base has 3n edges: n on each end, plus n joining the ends.
So 3n = 18, which gives n = 18 ÷ 3 = 6.
A base with 6 sides is a hexagon.

mistakes.A: Step 1: you divided by 2. A prism has 3 edges for each side of the base (n on each end plus n joining them), so divide by 3.
mistakes.B: Step 1: you used the faces rule (n + 2). The question gives edges, and a prism has 3n edges.
mistakes.D: Step 2: the 3 in 3n is not the base. Solve 3n = 18 to find how many sides the base has.

questions.topic: Angles at a point and vertically opposite angles
questions.prompt: Three angles sit side by side on a straight line: (x + 10)°, 2x° and (x + 30)°. Find x.
questions.explanation: The angles add to 180°: 4x + 40 = 180, so 4x = 140 and x = 35. x = 140 forgets to divide by 4.
steps: Angles on a straight line add to 180°, so (x + 10) + 2x + (x + 30) = 180.
Collect like terms: 4x + 40 = 180.
Subtract 40 from both sides: 4x = 140.
Divide both sides by 4: x = 35. Check: 45 + 70 + 65 = 180 ✓

mistakes.A: Step 1: you used 360°. Angles on a straight line add to 180°.
mistakes.C: Step 3: you added 40 instead of subtracting it. To undo '+ 40', take 40 from both sides.
mistakes.D: Step 4: 4x = 140 is not finished. Divide both sides by 4.

questions.prompt: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 6. What is the largest angle?
questions.explanation: There are 1 + 2 + 6 = 9 parts sharing 180°, so one part is 20° and the largest angle is 6 × 20° = 120°. 20° is only one part.
steps: Total parts: 1 + 2 + 6 = 9.
The angles add to 180°, so one part = 180° ÷ 9 = 20°.
Largest angle = 6 parts = 6 × 20° = 120°. Check: 20 + 40 + 120 = 180 ✓

mistakes.B: Step 3: 20° is one part, which is the smallest angle. The largest angle is 6 parts.
mistakes.C: Step 1: 1 + 2 + 6 = 9 parts, not 8. Count the total parts again.
mistakes.D: Step 2: you shared 360° instead of 180°. The angles of a triangle add to 180°.

questions.prompt: In a parallelogram, one angle is 4 times the size of an angle next to it. What size is the larger angle?
questions.explanation: Angles next to each other in a parallelogram add to 180°, so x + 4x = 180, x = 36 and the larger angle is 4 × 36° = 144°. 36° is the smaller angle.
steps: Call the smaller angle x, so the larger one is 4x.
Angles next to each other in a parallelogram are co-interior, so they add to 180°: x + 4x = 180, so 5x = 180.
Divide by 5: x = 36.
Larger angle = 4 × 36° = 144°. Check: 36 + 144 = 180 ✓

mistakes.A: Step 3: 36° is the smaller angle. The larger angle is 4 times as big.
mistakes.B: Step 1: two angles next to each other in a parallelogram add to 180°, not 360°.
mistakes.C: Step 2: you wrote 4x = 180. The two angles are x and 4x, so x + 4x = 5x = 180.
